sheets.title: Settings › Keybindings — 1280 × 900
sheets.caption: Before, keybindings were the last panel of Settings › General: a YAML textarea that could remap five commands. After, Keybindings is its own tab: every command in the shell (30 on this plan), each with its keys as keycaps, a find field that also searches by pressing keys, the view filter, a reset, and the WCAG 2.1.4 single-character-keys switch.
sheets.before: tabs: General · Security · Vaults · Capabilities · Danger; one textarea, 0 keycaps
sheets.after: tabs: General · Keybindings · Security · Vaults · Capabilities · Danger; 30 command rows + 6 fixed, every key a keycap

sheets.title: Recording a key that is taken — 1280 × 900
sheets.caption: After only: the j keycap of Next row is pressed and k is recorded in its place. k belongs to Previous row, so nothing is overwritten: the row names the holder and offers swap, take, or keep. Before, the same screen had no keycaps to press.
sheets.after: mark: "k is taken by Previous row"; keys: swap · take · keep

sheets.title: Recording a macro — 1280 × 900
sheets.caption: After only: a new macro named triage, run when the vault unlocks, records gg 3j / y. The recorder reads the presses as the shell would, with the person's own keys — j was swapped onto Previous row on the sheet before, so 3j records as 3 × Previous row — and leaves out y (Copy secret), which an event may never run, naming it with a mark.
sheets.after: steps: First row, or row N · 3 × Previous row · Search this pane; mark: "Left out: item.copy-secret"

sheets.title: Settings › Keybindings — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: At phone width the name takes the row and the keys share the line under it; every keycap is a 44 × 44 target.
